propositions: The caused_by auto-derivation mechanism (file-level git blame over impacted paths) has not been directly measured for accuracy against proven root causes in the codebase's dominant defect shapes (unmet obligations, carrier commits, omissions).

Of 88 closed bugs carrying a caused_by edge, the deriver reproduces the recorded edge in 38 cases (agree), diverges in 6 (disagree), and abstains in 44 (50% fail-closed); agreement bounds but does not identify blame-derivation due to absence of a provenance marker on link events.

Against 8 independently proven root causes, the deriver reproduced zero correct attributions; abstained in 7 cases; and named a wrong target (innocent producer) in 1 case where it should have abstained.

Caused_by edges carry no provenance field distinguishing blame-derived from explicitly supplied attributions, making the metric's confidence unobservable to consumers (escape-rate lenses, epic-close floor).

The dominant defect shapes in this codebase (unmet obligation, carrier commit, omission) are structurally hard for file-level blame; history drift (commits no longer resolving, paths renamed/deleted, reformat carriers) confounds accuracy measurement at close time vs today.
